subject: ice storm power lines
title: What If It Rained Ice for Five Days? In 1998 Canada's Power Grid Fell Over

scenes.text: What if freezing rain fell for five days straight? In 1998 it brought down a power grid.
January 4, 1998. Rain falls on Quebec, Ontario and the northeastern US and freezes onto everything, until January 10.
Up to 100 millimetres of ice, double what the region gets in a normal year. Branches carry 70 to 110 millimetres and snap.
Over 1,000 steel pylons crumple in chain reactions. 30,000 wooden poles fall. Four million people lose power, some for a month.
Sixteen thousand soldiers deploy, the most since the Korean War. Around 30 people die. The bill: roughly five billion dollars.
South of Montreal they called it the Triangle of Darkness. Not from a blizzard. From rain that froze the moment it landed.

description:
What if rain froze onto everything for five days? From 4 to 10 January 1998 an ice storm dropped up to 100 mm of freezing rain on Quebec, Ontario and the northeastern US, about double the region's normal yearly total.
More than 1,000 transmission towers and 30,000 utility poles collapsed, over 4 million people lost power, some for a month, about 16,000 Canadian soldiers were deployed, around 30 people died and the cost ran to roughly $5 billion.
What should we run through next?
